She ----18---- taking care of her vegetables. She does not like to sit in the house ----19---- play games on the phone. She hopes to sell her harvest ----20---- month.

ctx-eng-q30.title:
Question 30
Read the following paragraph and answer question 30.
ctx-eng-q30.text: Nasir, Banda and Lona are friends. They all play football. Nasir also plays volleyball. Lona also plays netball.

ctx-eng-q13-15.title:
Questions 13 to 15
Read the story below and then answer questions 13 to 15.
ctx-eng-q13-15.text:
Many afternoons, Hyena and Hare spent hours in a field eating the farmer's groundnuts. One day, Hare heard that the farmer was complaining that his groundnuts were being stolen. Hare went to him and said, "I will catch the thief for you."

One afternoon, Hare told Hyena that groundnuts are sweeter when you eat them with your legs buried in the ground. Hyena buried his four legs in the ground. He looked at the Hare and asked him, "Hare, why have you not buried your four legs?" Hare replied, "My legs are very short." Hyena was happy with Hare's answer, and he continued eating groundnuts. Hare watched carefully and when he saw the farmer coming, he quickly ran away. Hyena too saw the farmer, and tried to escape, but his legs were stuck in the ground. The farmer caught him and gave him a thorough beating.

ctx-eng-q10-12.title:
Questions 10 to 12
Read the story below and then answer questions 10 to 12.
ctx-eng-q10-12.text:
Hassan likes running errands for his parents. The other day, he was sent to the shop to buy some items. His father had written the prices of the items on a list. The total cost was four hundred and twenty five shillings. His father had given him five hundred shillings. Hassan was expecting a balance of seventy five shillings.

The shopkeeper was very busy on that day. She was serving many customers. When Hassan got the balance, he stepped out of the shop to count the money. He could not believe it. The shopkeeper had given him five hundred and seventy five shillings! Hassan thought this was his lucky day.

He sat down under a tree to plan how he would spend his new found cash. He started counting all the things he wanted to buy. This time he would go to a different shop.

On his way to the shop, Hassan remembered what his father had once told him, "Never take what does not belong to you". He realised the five hundred shillings belonged to the shopkeeper. He walked back to the shop to return the money. The shopkeeper was surprised to see him back so soon. When Hassan handed her the money, she was very grateful and said, "You are an angel. I'm proud of you, young man".

Hassan walked home shoulder high. He knew his father would be very pleased with him.

ctx-eng-q6-9.title:
Questions 6 to 9
Read the passage below and then answer questions 6 to 9.
ctx-eng-q6-9.text:
Human beings have always kept animals for different purposes. Animals can be kept as pets. A pet is an animal kept for pleasure. We keep pets because we love their company. We play with them. They are just like our friends, so we keep them happy and comfortable. Indeed, the dog, which is a common pet, has been said to be man's best friend.

Animals can also be kept to help human beings do certain tasks. This is because they have **special** abilities which human beings do not have. For example, donkeys have strength to carry heavy luggage. They can therefore help us in transportation.

Some animals are kept as source of food. Animal products such as milk and eggs are a rich source of nutrients. It is important to realise that whether we keep animals as pets, to help in work, or for food, they deserve kind treatment.

ctx-eng-q1-3.title:
Questions 1 to 3
Read the telephone conversation below. It contains blank spaces numbered 1 to 3. For each blank space, select the best alternative from the choices given.
ctx-eng-q1-3.text:
**Pupil:** Hello, Teacher.

**Class teacher:** Hello, ----1----.

**Pupil:** I am Barasa Kabengi, a pupil in Grade 6 Yellow.

**Class teacher:** Yes, Barasa, how can I help you?

**Pupil:** ----2----.

**Class teacher:** Is there a problem at home?

**Pupil:** My young sister is joining Grade 1 today. She has been crying. She wants me to accompany her to school. Grade 1 learners are to report at 8:30 a.m. today.

**Class teacher:** Okay, Barasa. You can come along with her. Make sure you come to see me after she settles down in her classroom.

**Pupil:** ----3----.

sectionA.questionText: Fill in blank 1:

options.text: Whom do you want to speak to?

sectionA.explanation:
The correct answer is **Whom am I speaking to?**

**Analysis of the Correct Answer:**
In polite telephone conversations (especially when speaking to an elder, authority figure, or teacher), asking "Whom am I speaking to?" is the most formal and respectful way to inquire about the caller's identity. In grammar, "whom" is used because it acts as the object of the preposition "to" (as in, "I am speaking to whom?").

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **Who are you?:** This is too abrupt, rude, and informal for a teacher to say in a polite phone conversation.
* **Who is this?:** This is very casual and informal. It lacks the professional respect required in a school context.
* **Whom do you want to speak to?:** This reverses the roles. Barasa (the pupil) is the one calling the teacher, so the teacher needs to ask who is on the line, not whom the caller wants to talk to.

📌 **Key Learning Note:**
When asking for someone's identity on the phone in formal English, use "Whom am I speaking to?" or "May I know who is calling?".

sectionA.questionText: Fill in blank 2:

options.text: May I be late for school today?
I want to be late for school today.
I will be late for school today.
Must I be late for school today?

sectionA.explanation:
The correct answer is **May I be late for school today?**

**Analysis of the Correct Answer:**
The modal verb **"May"** is used to ask for permission politely from a teacher or an authority figure. Barasa needs permission from his class teacher to arrive late so he can accompany his young sister on her first day of Grade 1.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **I want to be late for school today.:** This states a personal desire rather than asking for permission politely.
* **I will be late for school today.:** This is a direct command/statement declaring that he will be late, without asking the teacher's permission first.
* **Must I be late for school today?:** This asks if being late is a compulsory requirement or obligation, which does not make sense here.

📌 **Key Learning Note:**
Always use **"May I..."** when asking for permission from teachers, parents, or elders.

sectionA.questionText: Fill in blank 3:
sectionA.explanation:
The correct answer is **Thank you, Teacher.**

**Analysis of the Correct Answer:**
Whenever someone grants your request or offers help, social dialogue etiquette requires you to express gratitude. Since the teacher agreed to let Barasa come late with his sister, the proper response is to thank the teacher.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **That's good, Teacher.:** This sounds like you are evaluating or grading the teacher's response rather than showing gratitude.
* **It's okay, Teacher.:** This is informal and sounds like you are forgiving someone or accepting an apology, not showing appreciation.
* **It's alright, Teacher.:** This is used to reassure someone or accept an apology, which is inappropriate after receiving permission.

📌 **Key Learning Note:**
Always say **"Thank you"** whenever a teacher or elder grants a request or helps you out.

sectionA.questionText:
For questions 4 to 5, complete each of the blank spaces with the correct alternative from the choices given.

4. If I had a lot of money, I ------- travel all over the world.
sectionA.explanation:
The correct answer is **would**.

**Analysis of the Correct Answer:**
This question tests the **Second Conditional** in English grammar, which is used for hypothetical or imaginary situations in the present or future. The rule for the Second Conditional is:
`If + Past Simple (had), ... WOULD + base verb (travel)`.
Since the sentence imagines something that is not currently true ("If I had a lot of money..."), we use **would**.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **should:** Used for giving advice or expressing duty/obligation, not for conditional imaginary outcomes.
* **can:** Used for present ability in real situations, whereas past conditional clauses require the past modal "would".
* **will:** Used in the First Conditional for real/likely future possibilities (`If I have money, I will travel...`).

📌 **Key Learning Note:**
Second Conditional Rule: `If + Past Simple (had), ... WOULD + verb (travel)`.

sectionA.questionText: 5. Odoko goes to school ------- foot every morning.
sectionA.explanation:
The correct answer is **on**.

**Analysis of the Correct Answer:**
In English grammar, prepositions of transport have fixed rules. We say **by car**, **by bus**, **by train**, or **by plane** when referring to vehicles. However, when talking about walking, the only correct idiomatic expression is strictly **on foot**.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **by:** Used for vehicles and mechanical modes of transport (e.g. **by bus**, **by bicycle**), but never for walking on your feet.
* **with:** Used to show the instrument used to perform an action (e.g. **cut with a knife**), not for walking.
* **in:** Used for being inside enclosed transport (e.g. **in a car**, **in a taxi**).

📌 **Key Learning Note:**
Always say **"on foot"** when referring to walking to school or any destination.

sectionA.questionText: 6. Why do we keep pets?

options.text: To help us carry heavy things.

sectionA.explanation:
The correct answer is **To make us happy.**

**Analysis of the Correct Answer:**
Paragraph 1 of the passage explicitly defines a pet as an animal kept for pleasure and companionship: **"We keep pets because we love their company... They are just like our friends, so we keep them happy and comfortable."** Keeping pets brings joy and happiness to our lives.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **To help us carry heavy things.:** The passage states that work animals like donkeys are kept to carry heavy luggage, not pets.
* **To provide food.:** Paragraph 3 explains that livestock (like cows and chickens) are kept as a source of food (milk and eggs), not pets.
* **To protect the environment.:** Protecting the environment is not mentioned in the passage as a reason for keeping pets.

📌 **Key Learning Note:**
Pets are kept for pleasure, love, and companionship ("to make us happy"), while work animals are kept to assist with heavy labor.

sectionA.questionText: 7. Which one of the following is **true** about donkeys and dogs?

options.text: They can do things that we cannot do.
They are always comfortable and healthy.

sectionA.explanation:
The correct answer is **They can do things that we cannot do.**

**Analysis of the Correct Answer:**
Paragraph 2 explicitly states: **"This is because they have special abilities which human beings do not have. For example, donkeys have strength to carry heavy luggage."** This confirms that animals can perform tasks and have physical capabilities beyond human abilities.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **They are man's best friend.:** Paragraph 1 specifically states that only the **dog** has been said to be man's best friend, not donkeys.
* **They are better than us.:** The text does not claim that animals are superior to humans overall.
* **They are always comfortable and healthy.:** Paragraph 1 states that **we** must make sure to keep them happy and comfortable, not that they are always comfortable on their own.

📌 **Key Learning Note:**
Animals assist humans because they possess unique physical abilities (such as strength or heightened senses) that humans lack.

sectionA.questionText: 8. The word **'special'** as used in the passage means the same as
sectionA.explanation:
The correct answer is **unusual.**

**Analysis of the Correct Answer:**
In Paragraph 2, the phrase **"special abilities"** refers to extraordinary, uncommon, or exceptional traits that set animals apart from humans. Among the given choices, **unusual** best matches this meaning of being remarkable or out of the ordinary.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **strange.:** This implies odd or weird in a negative way, which does not fit the positive context of helpful animal abilities.
* **new.:** Means recently acquired or created, which does not mean exceptional or unique.
* **unknown.:** Means unfamiliar or obscure, whereas these animal abilities are well known to humans.

📌 **Key Learning Note:**
Contextual vocabulary: In this context, "special" means uncommon, extraordinary, or **unusual** abilities.

sectionA.questionText: 9. What is likely to happen if we do not treat animals kindly?

options.text: They will not live with us.
They may not give us enough food.
We may not get enough benefits from them.
We may not be happy and comfortable.

sectionA.explanation:
The correct answer is **We may not get enough benefits from them.**

**Analysis of the Correct Answer:**
Paragraph 3 emphasizes that all animals—whether kept as pets, work animals, or food sources—deserve kind treatment. If we mistreat them, pets will not provide joyful companionship, work animals will grow weak or fall ill, and food animals will produce fewer products. Thus, we will lose out on their maximum benefits.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **They will not live with us.:** Domestic animals may remain in captivity even if mistreated, so leaving is not the direct main consequence.
* **They may not give us enough food.:** This only applies to livestock (milk/eggs), whereas the question asks about all domestic animals generally.
* **We may not be happy and comfortable.:** This focuses only on pets, rather than the total practical benefits lost across all types of animals.

📌 **Key Learning Note:**
Treating animals kindly ensures they stay healthy, productive, and able to provide us with maximum benefits.

sectionA.questionText: 10. Why did Hassan's father write the list of items?

options.text: He did not want Hassan to forget any item.
He did not want Hassan to delay in the shop.
He wanted Hassan to get the right balance from the shopkeeper.
He wanted Hassan to do the totals of the cost of the items.

sectionA.explanation:
The correct answer is **He wanted Hassan to get the right balance from the shopkeeper.**

**Analysis of the Correct Answer:**
In Paragraph 1, the story states that Hassan's father wrote the prices on a list, calculating the total cost (425 shillings) from a 500-shilling note. This enabled Hassan to calculate and expect the exact balance of 75 shillings, ensuring he received the right change from the shopkeeper.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **He did not want Hassan to forget any item.:** The prices were written specifically so Hassan could know the exact total cost and expected balance.
* **He did not want Hassan to delay in the shop.:** Saving time was not stated as the primary reason for writing down the prices.
* **He wanted Hassan to do the totals of the cost of the items.:** Hassan's father had already calculated the total cost (425 shillings) and balance on the list.

📌 **Key Learning Note:**
Writing down item prices helps buyers verify total costs and ensure they receive the exact correct change/balance.

sectionA.questionText: 11. The shopkeeper was surprised to see Hassan back because ---------

options.text: the shopkeeper was very busy that day.
Hassan had just left the shop.
the shopkeeper had given him the balance.

sectionA.explanation:
The correct answer is **Hassan had just left the shop.**

**Analysis of the Correct Answer:**
In Paragraph 4, the text states that Hassan stepped outside, sat under a tree right by the shop, counted the money, remembered his father's advice, and walked straight back to return the extra 500 shillings. The shopkeeper was surprised because Hassan had literally just walked out seconds before and returned so quickly.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **Hassan returned the money.:** Returning the extra cash explains why she felt grateful ("You are an angel"), but seeing him return **so quickly** (just after leaving) is what surprised her initially.
* **the shopkeeper was very busy that day.:** Being busy explains why she made the mistake in giving change, not why she was surprised by his quick return.
* **the shopkeeper had given him the balance.:** Giving change was part of her normal work, not a cause of surprise.

📌 **Key Learning Note:**
The shopkeeper was surprised by Hassan's immediate return right after stepping out of the shop.

sectionA.questionText: 12. This story teaches us that ---------

options.text: a friend in need is a friend indeed.

sectionA.explanation:
The correct answer is **honesty is the best policy.**

**Analysis of the Correct Answer:**
The main moral of Hassan's story is honesty. Even though Hassan had the chance to keep 500 extra shillings without anyone knowing, he remembered his father's teaching ("Never take what does not belong to you") and returned the money. His honest decision earned him praise, respect, and a peaceful conscience.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **hurry hurry has no blessing.:** This proverb warns against rushing foolishly, which is unrelated to returning extra change.
* **once bitten twice shy.:** This means being cautious after experiencing a bad situation, which does not apply here.
* **a friend in need is a friend indeed.:** This refers to true friends helping each other in tough times, which does not fit the transaction with the shopkeeper.

📌 **Key Learning Note:**
Returning money or items that do not belong to you illustrates the timeless moral: **Honesty is the best policy**.

sectionA.questionText: 13. Which one of the following is **true** according to the story?

options.text: Hare stole the groundnuts just like Hyena.
Hare was a true friend of the farmer.
Hare was not able to cheat Hyena.
Hare buried one of his legs in the ground.

sectionA.explanation:
The correct answer is **Hare stole the groundnuts just like Hyena.**

**Analysis of the Correct Answer:**
Paragraph 1 states: **"Many afternoons, Hyena and Hare spent hours in a field eating the farmer's groundnuts."** Both animals were stealing and eating the farmer's crops without permission.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **Hare was a true friend of the farmer.:** Hare went to the farmer pretending to help catch the thief, but he was actually the thief deceiving the farmer.
* **Hare was not able to cheat Hyena.:** Hare successfully tricked Hyena into burying his legs in the soil so Hyena couldn't run away.
* **Hare buried one of his legs in the ground.:** Hare lied that his legs were too short and did not bury any of his legs.

📌 **Key Learning Note:**
Both Hare and Hyena were crop thieves, but Hare used trickery to escape while leaving Hyena to get caught.

sectionA.questionText: 14. From the story, Hare is ---------.
sectionA.explanation:
The correct answer is **tricky**.

**Analysis of the Correct Answer:**
Throughout the story, Hare acts with cunning deceit. He tricks Hyena into burying all four legs in the dirt so Hyena becomes trapped, while Hare stays free to run away when the farmer approaches. This defines Hare as **tricky** (cunning/sly).

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **friendly:** Hare betrayed his companion Hyena to save himself, showing he was not a genuine friend.
* **funny:** Although the story is humorous, Hare's central character trait is being sly and tricky.
* **busy:** Hare spent his time stealing crops and plotting tricks rather than doing honest work.

📌 **Key Learning Note:**
In traditional African folktales, the Hare is typically portrayed as a cunning and **tricky** character.

sectionA.questionText: 15. What do we learn from this story?

options.text: People need to share what they have.
We should keep the right friends.
We should always do what we are told.

sectionA.explanation:
The correct answer is **We should keep the right friends.**

**Analysis of the Correct Answer:**
Hyena trusted Hare as a companion, but Hare tricked him into burying his legs, abandoned him, and left him to take a beating from the farmer. This story teaches us to be careful about who we associate with, as untrustworthy friends will betray us in times of trouble.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **People need to share what they have.:** The story is about theft and trickery, not generous sharing.
* **Farmers should beat all Hyenas.:** The moral lesson of a folktale is about human character and wisdom, not physically beating wild animals.
* **We should always do what we are told.:** Blindly obeying bad advice (like Hyena obeying Hare's instruction to bury his legs) leads to disaster.

📌 **Key Learning Note:**
Be wise when choosing companions: keeping untrustworthy or deceitful friends leads to betrayal and trouble.

sectionA.questionText: 16. Asha has a small garden at home. She likes it because it is a gift from ----16---- grandfather.
sectionA.explanation:
The correct answer is **her**.

**Analysis of the Correct Answer:**
Possessive adjectives show ownership before a noun. Since Asha is a female person (singular female subject pronoun **she**), the corresponding possessive adjective for her grandfather is **her** (**her grandfather**).

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **his:** Possessive adjective used for a male person (e.g. **his grandfather**).
* **hers:** Possessive pronoun used without a noun following it (e.g. **the garden is hers**), whereas here it precedes the noun **grandfather**.
* **him:** Object pronoun (e.g. **I called him**), not a possessive adjective.

📌 **Key Learning Note:**
Use **her** as a possessive adjective before a noun when referring to a female person (e.g. **her book**, **her garden**, **her grandfather**).

sectionA.questionText: 17. Asha grows ----17---- vegetables in her garden.
sectionA.explanation:
The correct answer is **different**.

**Analysis of the Correct Answer:**
In the context of growing crops in a garden, the adjective **different** is used to describe growing various types or kinds of healthy vegetables (such as spinach, kales, carrots, and onions).

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **dry:** Living, growing vegetables in a garden are fresh and watered, not dry.
* **cooked:** Vegetables grow raw in the soil; they are only cooked after harvesting.
* **plenty:** Requires the preposition "of" to function correctly as a determiner (**plenty of vegetables**), so it cannot directly modify "vegetables" here.

📌 **Key Learning Note:**
"Different vegetables" means various types of healthy crops growing together in a garden.

sectionA.questionText: 18. She ----18---- taking care of her vegetables.
sectionA.explanation:
The correct answer is **enjoys**.

**Analysis of the Correct Answer:**
Contextual verbs express feelings towards an activity. The passage states Asha likes her garden and prefers working in it over sitting inside playing phone games. Therefore, she **enjoys** taking care of her vegetables.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **begins:** Refers only to starting an action, which does not convey her affection or passion for gardening.
* **accepts:** Means agreeing to receive something, which does not make sense with taking care of vegetables.
* **admires:** Means looking at something with appreciation, whereas taking care of a garden is active labor (**enjoys taking care**).

📌 **Key Learning Note:**
Phrasing like "enjoys taking care of" shows active pleasure and dedication in looking after something.

sectionA.questionText: 19. She does not like to sit in the house ----19---- play games on the phone.
sectionA.explanation:
The correct answer is **and**.

**Analysis of the Correct Answer:**
The coordinating conjunction **and** is used to connect two related indoor activities that Asha dislikes doing: **sitting in the house** AND **playing games on the phone**. 

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **also:** An adverb used for adding information, requiring a different sentence structure.
* **yet:** A contrasting conjunction meaning "but", which is incorrect because both activities are complementary indoor actions.
* **because:** A causal conjunction used to introduce a reason, not to link two parallel actions.

📌 **Key Learning Note:**
Use **and** to join two related or parallel activities in a single clause.

sectionA.questionText: 20. She hopes to sell her harvest ----20---- month.
sectionA.explanation:
The correct answer is **next**.

**Analysis of the Correct Answer:**
When expressing expectations about an upcoming time period in English, we use the adjective **next**. Therefore, "sell her harvest **next month**" correctly refers to the month immediately following the present one.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **future:** Needs a prepositional phrase like **in the future** or an adjective like **future plans**, not **future month**.
* **new:** Refers to something recently created or acquired, not a coming calendar month.
* **later:** An adverb requiring a phrase like **later this month**, not **later month**.

📌 **Key Learning Note:**
Use **next month**, **next week**, or **next year** to refer to upcoming calendar time periods.

sectionA.questionText: 21. The teacher found the learner ------- the classroom.
sectionA.explanation:
The correct answer is **in**.

**Analysis of the Correct Answer:**
Prepositions of place indicate location. When someone or something is located inside an enclosed 3D space, room, or building, we use the preposition **in** (**in the classroom**).

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **to:** Indicates movement or direction towards a destination (e.g. **walking to the classroom**).
* **on:** Indicates position resting on a flat surface (e.g. **on the roof**).
* **over:** Indicates a position directly above something without touching it (e.g. **flew over the classroom**).

📌 **Key Learning Note:**
Use **in** for enclosed locations like rooms, classrooms, houses, and buildings.

sectionA.questionText: 22. Ali left the book ------- the table.
sectionA.explanation:
The correct answer is **on**.

**Analysis of the Correct Answer:**
Prepositions of surface location describe where an object rests. When an item rests upon the top flat surface of a piece of furniture, we use **on** (**on the table**).

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **with:** Indicates companionship or tool used (e.g. **with a pen**).
* **in:** Means inside an enclosed space (e.g. **in the drawer**).
* **from:** Indicates origin or starting point (e.g. **from the library**).

📌 **Key Learning Note:**
Use **on** when an object is resting on top of a flat surface like a table, desk, or floor.

sectionA.questionText: 23. The children are planting trees, -------
sectionA.explanation:
The correct answer is **aren't they?**

**Analysis of the Correct Answer:**
Question tags follow three main grammar rules:
1. **Positive statement ➔ Negative tag.** The sentence "The children are planting trees" is positive.
2. **Match the auxiliary verb.** The auxiliary verb is **are**, so the negative form is **aren't**.
3. **Match the pronoun.** The subject "The children" is third-person plural, replaced by **they**.
Putting it together gives the tag **aren't they?**.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **aren't we?:** Changes the pronoun from third-person plural (**they**) to first-person plural (**we**).
* **are they?:** Uses a positive tag, which is incorrect for a positive statement.
* **are we?:** Uses a positive tag and an incorrect pronoun.

📌 **Key Learning Note:**
Question Tag Rule: Positive statement + Positive verb ("are") ➔ Negative tag ("aren't they?").

sectionA.questionText: 24. Rudisha did not find the story book in his bag because ------- had taken it.
sectionA.explanation:
The correct answer is **somebody**.

**Analysis of the Correct Answer:**
Indefinite pronouns refer to unspecified people:
- **Somebody / Someone**: Used in affirmative (positive) clauses when referring to an unknown person who took an action.
Because the clause "...because somebody had taken it" is a positive statement explaining why the book was missing, **somebody** is the correct pronoun.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **anybody:** Used in negative statements (**did not see anybody**) or questions (**did anybody take it?**).
* **everybody:** Means all people, which makes no sense because multiple people wouldn't take a single book.
* **nobody:** Means no person; saying "nobody had taken it" would contradict why the book was missing from the bag.

📌 **Key Learning Note:**
Use **somebody** in positive statement clauses when referring to an unknown person.

sectionA.questionText: 25. The teacher told us to take care of ------- during the journey.
sectionA.explanation:
The correct answer is **ourselves**.

**Analysis of the Correct Answer:**
Reflexive pronouns refer back to the subject or object of the clause:
- Subject/Object **we / us** (1st person plural) ➔ Reflexive pronoun **ourselves**.
Since the teacher told **us** (first-person plural) to take care of a group including ourselves, the correct reflexive pronoun is **ourselves**.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **themselves:** Reflexive pronoun for **they/them** (3rd person plural).
* **yourself:** Singular reflexive pronoun for **you** (2nd person singular).
* **yourselves:** Plural reflexive pronoun for **you all** (2nd person plural).

📌 **Key Learning Note:**
Reflexive pronoun pairing: **we / us ➔ ourselves**.

sectionA.questionText: 26. The thieves took away our goats ------- force.
sectionA.explanation:
The correct answer is **by**.

**Analysis of the Correct Answer:**
Prepositional phrases indicating manner or method follow fixed idiomatic expressions. The standard English expression meaning using physical compulsion or violence is **by force** (**took away our goats by force**).

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **with:** Used for instruments (e.g. **cut with a knife**), not in the phrase **by force**.
* **at:** Used for location or time (e.g. **at noon**), not manner.
* **under:** Used in phrases like **under pressure** or **under arrest**, but not **by force**.

📌 **Key Learning Note:**
The correct fixed idiomatic prepositional phrase is **by force**.

sectionA.questionText: 27. This is the hen ------- egg broke.
sectionA.explanation:
The correct answer is **whose**.

**Analysis of the Correct Answer:**
Relative pronouns link clauses by indicating identity or possession:
- **whose**: Shows possession for people, animals, or objects (**the hen whose egg broke** = the egg belonging to the hen).

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **who:** Subject pronoun used for human beings (e.g. **the teacher who taught us**).
* **whom:** Object pronoun used for human beings (e.g. **the man whom I met**).
* **which:** Used for non-possessive references to animals or things (e.g. **the hen which laid an egg**).

📌 **Key Learning Note:**
Use **whose** to show possession for people, animals, or things.

sectionA.questionText: 28. The class teacher will ------- us a present.
sectionA.explanation:
The correct answer is **give**.

**Analysis of the Correct Answer:**
Modal auxiliary verbs (**will, shall, can, may, must, should, would**) must ALWAYS be followed by the **bare infinitive** (the base form of the main verb without 'to').
Therefore, after the modal **will**, the base verb **give** is required (**will give**).

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **given:** Past participle form (**has given**), which cannot follow a modal verb directly.
* **gives:** Third-person singular present form (**he gives**), which cannot follow a modal verb.
* **gave:** Simple past tense form (**he gave**), which cannot follow a modal verb.

📌 **Key Learning Note:**
Grammar Rule: Modal verbs (will, shall, can, may) + Base Verb (**will give**).

sectionA.questionText:
29. 'Neither Kalusi nor Sofia came late to class'.
Means:

options.text: Only Kalusi came late to class.
Only Sofia came late to class.
Both Kalusi and Sofia came late to class.
Both Kalusi and Sofia did not come late to class.

sectionA.explanation:
The correct answer is **Both Kalusi and Sofia did not come late to class.**

**Analysis of the Correct Answer:**
Correlative conjunctions **Neither ... nor** mean "not the one and not the other". They negate both persons or items mentioned in the sentence.
Therefore, "Neither Kalusi nor Sofia came late" means that Kalusi did NOT come late, and Sofia did NOT come late either (both were on time).

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **Only Kalusi came late to class.:** Incorrectly claims one student was late.
* **Only Sofia came late to class.:** Incorrectly claims the other student was late.
* **Both Kalusi and Sofia came late to class.:** Reverses the meaning into a positive statement of lateness for both students.

📌 **Key Learning Note:**
"Neither A nor B" means **BOTH A and B did NOT** perform or experience the action.

sectionA.questionText: 30. According to the story, who plays football only?
sectionA.explanation:
The correct answer is **Banda.**

**Analysis of the Correct Answer:**
Reading logic puzzles requires carefully matching every condition in the text:
- **Nasir**: plays football AND volleyball.
- **Banda**: plays football ONLY.
- **Lona**: plays football AND netball.
Since Banda plays football and has no other additional sport listed, **Banda** is the only one who plays football **only**.

**Why Other Options Are Incorrect:**
* **Nasir.:** Plays football AND volleyball.
* **Lona.:** Plays football AND netball.
* **All of them.:** All three play football, but Nasir and Lona play other sports too, so they do not play football **only**.

📌 **Key Learning Note:**
Pay close attention to restrictive words like **"only"** when answering comprehension puzzles.
